value.title: Alternate launch configs per harness (`--alt`)
value.summary: `pij-rs spawn --alt <name>` launches a harness with an alternate config from `~/.pij-rs/harness-alts.toml` (env, bin, args). The seat records the alt; revive re-reads and reuses it, refusing if it is gone; a Claude alt's home is where the binder looks for the seat. Doctor reports alts. F280.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Jordan runs a second Claude Code setup through a shell function (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.claude-alt" claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`). pij can adopt such a seat but cannot spawn one, and revive relaunches it as plain `claude` in the default home, where `--resume` misses its transcript. This plan adds named alternate launches per harness in one TOML file, a `--alt` spawn flag, the alt recorded on the seat and reused by revive, and the Claude binder reading the alt's home.

sections.name: goals
value: Any harness can be started an alternate way by name, configured once in pij.
A seat started with an alt is revived with the same alt, or refused loudly, never relaunched with the default.
A Claude alt seat binds and resumes in its own home.

sections.name: non_goals
value: No per-alt model, effort or role defaults: those stay spawn flags.
No `--alt` on revive to change a seat's alt.
No removal of the existing `~/.claude-alt` probe in `claude_homes_from` (proposed to the prime separately).
No hook install into a home configured after the daemon started: that happens at the next daemon start, and doctor says so.
No `pij-rs doctor harness-alts` verb (scope cut by the prime, 2026-11-22).

value.claim: `<state-dir>/harness-alts.toml` (`~/.pij-rs/harness-alts.toml`) holds one table per alternate launch, `[<harness>.<name>]`, with optional `env` (a string table), `bin` (an absolute executable) and `args` (strings appended to the launch). A leading `~` in an env value or `bin` is the user's home. A missing file means no alts. The file is refused whole, naming the file and the fault, for an unknown harness key or field, an alt name outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,32}`, an env key outside `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` or starting `PIJ_`, a control character in any value, a relative `bin`, or a relative Claude `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. The config layer knows no harness's variables except where a Claude home is read (ac-0005).

`pij-rs spawn --harness <h> --alt <name>` launches with the alt's env (applied after `PIJ_SESSION_ID`/`PIJ_SPAWN_ID` and before pij's own harness env, so pij's own values win), its `bin` in place of the harness name, and its `args` after pij's own. An alt absent from the file refuses `E-RS-ALT-UNKNOWN`, naming the file and the harness's known alts; an unreadable or invalid file refuses `E-RS-ALT-CONFIG`; `--bin` with an alt that sets `bin` refuses. A refusal launches nothing and writes no row. A spawn without `--alt` is unchanged and does not read the file.

The seat records its alt as `alt: {name, home}` (`home`: the Claude home the alt's env names, else absent) in a new `seats.alt` column (migration 0051). Registration keeps it. `pij-rs state` shows it in the JSON and as an `alt:` line; `pij list` shows the harness cell as `<harness> alt:<name>` in both the Rust CLI and the TS shim (golden `list-sized`). A seat without an alt shows nothing new.

`pij-rs revive` of a seat with an alt relaunches with that alt, re-reading the file at revive time, so edits apply. If the alt is gone from the file, or the file is unreadable, the revive refuses (`E-RS-ALT-UNKNOWN` / `E-RS-ALT-CONFIG`) before any write: no tombstone, no launch, never the default launch. A seat without an alt revives as before without reading the file.

A pending spawned Claude seat whose alt names a Claude home binds from `<that home>/sessions`, not `~/.claude/sessions`; others are unchanged. `claude_homes()` also lists every existing Claude home named by a configured alt, so pij's hooks and inbound setting are installed there at daemon start and its transcripts and session records are read.

`pij-rs spawn --help` documents `--alt`, and `docs/how/pij-rs-api.md` gains a short Harness alts section (file, fields, precedence, refusals, revive, Claude home, cost). Doctor needs no new verb: an alt's Claude home is one of `claude_homes()`, so `just doctor`'s existing claude-hooks rows report its hooks with their fix.

Cost: no new loop, poll, timer or per-tick work, and no process launch. The file is read only by a spawn with `--alt` (once), a revive of a seat with an alt (twice: the pre-write check and the launch), each `claude_homes()` call (daemon start, CLI doctor commands, revive `--ask`/`--cheap`), and `doctor harness-alts`. The Claude binder still reads one sessions directory per pending seat per pass; only which directory changes.

Canary on the live daemon: an alt matching the operator's `cc-alt` (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-alt`; pij already passes `--dangerously-skip-permissions`) spawns a throwaway Claude seat from a scratch folder that binds, with its transcript under `~/.claude-alt/projects/`; after close, revive resumes the same session in the same home; then close. Nothing is added to or deleted from `~/.claude-alt` beyond what the seat writes.

value.title: Harness alts shipped
value.brief: All ACs, one PR (coder pij-musical-takin). Config module in pij-harnesses; SpawnRequest.alt; daemon resolves at spawn/revive; SeatAlt on the descriptor + migration 0051; binder home; state/list/doctor; docs; canary.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Code map (main 3707709e). Spawn argv: `pij_harnesses::build_spawn_plan` (crates/harnesses/src/spawn.rs) builds `env PIJ_SESSION_ID=.. PIJ_SPAWN_ID=.. [COPILOT_*] <harness> <args>`; `--bin` replaces the harness name after `validate_executable_override`. The daemon's `launch_owned` (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs) builds the plan and writes the descriptor; revive (crates/daemon/src/http/revive.rs) rebuilds a `SpawnRequest` from the prior row (`executable: None`, so `--bin` is not durable today). Durable per-seat launch facts precedent: `cache_proxy` (JSON TEXT column, migration 0047; `opted_out` survives revive). Registration clones the existing row, so a new descriptor field survives binding unless cleared. Claude binder (crates/daemon/src/claude_bind.rs `matching_record`) reads only `$HOME/.claude/sessions`. `claude_homes_from` already appends `~/.claude-alt` when it exists. Config precedent: `cache-proxy.toml` in the state dir, parsed with `toml` + `deny_unknown_fields`. The roster table is rendered by both `crates/cli/src/roster.rs` and `.omp/extensions/pij/core/roster-table.ts`, pinned by golden `list-sized`.

value.risk: An alt's env carries a secret (an API key) that then shows in a receipt or doctor.
value.mitigation: Only the alt name and the Claude home are recorded on the seat; doctor prints env keys, never values. The launch argv carries the env as `env` does today for pij's own variables (visible to `ps`), stated in the docs.

value.risk: An alt home configured after the daemon started lacks pij's hooks.
value.mitigation: The binder needs no hook (it reads Claude's own session record). `just doctor`'s claude-hooks rows list the home with its fix; docs say hooks land at the next daemon start.

value.risk: An edit moves an alt's Claude home, and revive then resumes in a home without the transcript.
value.mitigation: The brief asks that edits apply. Docs say so; the recorded home shows in `pij-rs state` so the change is visible.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Cargo only via `just shared-build` (niced, one at a time); never pkill or delete by pattern.
No operator login, email or machine path in committed files: examples use `~`.
`~/.claude-alt` is the operator's real setup: add nothing beyond what the canary seat writes, delete nothing.
